jobs.title: Research Scientist – Neuroscience
jobs.description:
The Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine at Stanford University School of Medicine is seeking a Research Scientist with a neuroscience background and expertise in electrophysiology, patch-clamp recording, and calcium imaging to join the Anderson Laboratory.

The Anderson Laboratory is a translational pain and neuromodulation laboratory investigating novel approaches to prevent and treat acute and chronic pain, with a major emphasis on diagnostic ultrasound-guided focused ultrasound for noninvasive peripheral nerve modulation. The laboratory integrates neuroscience, bioengineering, electrophysiology, behavioral models, imaging, and translational research to understand how focused ultrasound alters peripheral neural signaling and to develop this technology toward clinical application.

The Research Scientist will take a leading role in developing the laboratory's mechanistic neuroscience program. The individual will design and perform electrophysiologic and imaging experiments to determine how focused ultrasound and related interventions affect peripheral nerves and sensory neurons, with particular emphasis on neuronal excitability, nociceptive signaling, ion-channel function, and cellular responses.

The successful candidate will have substantial expertise in electrophysiology, patch clamp, and calcium imaging and will be expected to operate with considerable scientific independence. Responsibilities will include experimental design, development and optimization of new methodologies, execution and analysis of complex neuroscience experiments, interpretation of results, preparation of publications and grant applications, presentation of findings, and training and mentoring of junior research personnel.

This position provides an opportunity to participate in a highly multidisciplinary research program spanning fundamental neuroscience, bioengineering, preclinical models, and translation of novel neuromodulation technologies toward human studies.

**CORE DUTIES:**

Design and lead neuroscience experiments. Develop experimental strategies to investigate neuronal excitability, sensory signaling, peripheral nerve physiology, and mechanisms of neuromodulation. Independently establish experimental parameters, controls, endpoints, and analytical approaches.

Perform advanced electrophysiologic studies. Conduct electrophysiologic experiments including whole-cell and/or other patch-clamp recordings, extracellular electrophysiology, and related approaches to characterize neuronal membrane properties, ion-channel activity, action potential generation, synaptic or sensory signaling, and responses to experimental interventions.

Perform calcium imaging and functional neuronal imaging. Design and conduct calcium-imaging experiments in neuronal preparations; optimize acquisition protocols; perform quantitative image and signal analysis; and integrate imaging results with electrophysiologic and behavioral findings.

Analyze and interpret complex experimental data. Apply appropriate quantitative, statistical, electrophysiologic, and imaging analysis techniques. Integrate findings across experimental modalities and develop mechanistic hypotheses based on experimental results.

Develop and optimize experimental methods. Establish new techniques and protocols; troubleshoot instrumentation and experimental preparations; improve reproducibility and rigor; and recommend modifications to research approaches based on experimental findings and emerging scientific literature.

Scientific writing and dissemination. Contribute substantially to manuscripts, abstracts, presentations, research reports, and grant applications. Present research findings at laboratory meetings, departmental conferences, and scientific meetings.

Mentoring and scientific supervision. Train and mentor research assistants, graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and other laboratory personnel in electrophysiology, patch clamp, calcium imaging, experimental design, data analysis, and rigorous scientific practices.

Laboratory and collaborative activities. Participate in multidisciplinary collaborations, maintain appropriate experimental documentation and data integrity, assist with equipment and laboratory organization related to neuroscience studies, and contribute to regulatory and research-compliance activities.

**QUALIFICATIONS / MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

PhD in neuroscience, neurobiology, physiology, biomedical engineering, pharmacology, or a closely related discipline is strongly preferred. Candidates should have substantial research experience in neuroscience and demonstrated expertise in electrophysiologic methods.

Strong candidates will have significant hands-on experience with patch-clamp electrophysiology, preferably including whole-cell recordings from neurons; calcium imaging, including experimental acquisition and quantitative analysis; neuronal or peripheral nerve electrophysiology; experimental design and troubleshooting of technically complex neuroscience experiments; quantitative analysis of electrophysiologic and imaging datasets; and preparation of manuscripts for peer-reviewed publication.

Experience with sensory neuroscience, pain neuroscience, peripheral nerves, dorsal root ganglion neurons, ion channels, neuromodulation, ultrasound, or related areas would be particularly valuable. Experience with animal models and ex vivo or in vitro neuronal preparations is also desirable.

The expected pay range for this position is $80,000 to $100,000 per annum.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Research Scientist - Safety Environments
jobs.description:
**About Plato**
===============

Plato is an applied research lab building the foundational infrastructure to train specialized AI agents.

We turn real-world data streams into high-fidelity simulated environments that generate the training signal needed to make capable models. Our work supports frontier labs, hyperscalers, and enterprises building AI systems for complex, high-stakes work.

Today, only a handful of players can train models for capable work. Compute and algorithms are rapidly commoditizing, but reinforcement learning data remains the bottleneck. Plato is changing that by automatically scaling training environments from proprietary real-world data.

**Why Apply**
=============

* Work with the frontier: Build safety environments and benchmarks that research teams at leading AI labs can use to measure emerging capabilities and misaligned behavior.
* Real ownership: Help set Plato’s safety evaluation agenda, from the research questions worth testing to the evidence we share with lab partners.
* Research to production: Work with engineers to turn experimental designs into runnable environments, with a short path from an idea to an evaluation labs can use.

**The Role**
============

Plato is hiring an individual contributor researcher to design safety environments and benchmarks, starting with evaluations that measure how well AI models can improve themselves and other models.

You will establish a new research direction at Plato, designing safety-relevant benchmarks and working with engineers to turn them into runnable environments. Your initial focus will be measuring AI R&D capabilities, including experiment design, model training, and research replication.

You will also investigate reward hacking, sabotage, deception, and other misaligned behavior. The work spans research design, empirical evaluation, and failure analysis, with substantial ownership of the research agenda. Some environments may also be used in training to reduce the behaviors they reveal.

**What You’ll Do**
==================

* Design Safety Benchmarks: Measure AI research automation and self-improvement. Define tasks, baselines, budgets, and success criteria that separate meaningful progress from superficial completion.
* Build Safety Environments: Design environments that expose reward hacking, sabotage, deception, and failures to follow intended constraints.
* Hold the Evaluation Bar: Investigate contamination, grader weaknesses, task ambiguity, and shortcuts that could make a result misleading.
* Track Frontier Capabilities: Run experiments with current models, inspect trajectories and failures, and measure how capabilities change across models and over time.
* Work with Engineering: Turn research designs into reproducible environments with clear scoring, useful instrumentation, and documented limitations.
* Share the Findings: Translate results into benchmark releases, research reports, and concrete recommendations for lab partners.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Recent Research: Hands-on work in frontier-model evaluation, benchmarks, or AI safety in the past one to two years.
* Research Track Record: Meaningful contributions to papers, released benchmarks, public reports, or comparable empirical work. We care about the quality of your work and your contribution more than credentials or years of experience.
* Current Model Knowledge: Practical familiarity with current frontier models and a specific, evidence-based view of their capabilities, limitations, and likely development.
* Experimental Judgment: You can explain what an evaluation measures, how it could be gamed, and which conclusions its results do and do not support.
* Research Ownership: Ability to turn an ambiguous question into a concrete experimental design and collaborate closely with engineers to implement it.
* Safety Focus: Interest in measuring safety-relevant capabilities and behavior, including the tradeoffs when evaluation environments are also used for training.
* Bay Area Based: Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, or willing to relocate.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Designed and released a benchmark, particularly for AI R&D, long-horizon agents, dangerous capabilities, or AI control. Relevant reference points include RE-Bench, MLE-bench, and PaperBench.
* Experience in an independent evaluation or safety organization, a frontier lab safety team, or pre-deployment testing with labs or government evaluation bodies.
* Direct research on models conducting ML experiments, training or improving other models, replicating papers, or completing extended research tasks.
* A software engineering background or programming skills that let you implement environments, evaluation harnesses, and analysis tools yourself.
* Experience publishing rigorous empirical research, including work at major machine-learning venues.

Compensation Range: $275K - $450K

As a Principal Applied Scientist for the FAIM team, you will invent the models that help advertisers achieve desired outcomes. Today's state of the art models can setup ad campaigns to a specification, but do not understand advertising strategy well enough to help with abstract goals that real advertisers ask about like "how can I make more money."  
  
This is a rare charter to build foundational optimization science where little exists today, spanning campaign recommendation, cross-product budget allocation, incrementality measurement, and long-term-sales modeling. You will set technical direction for a growing team, partner with engineering and product to take models from research to production at Amazon scale, and directly move advertiser ROAS and new-to-brand growth.  
  
In this role you will
  

* Own the science vision for training models in our RL Gym from end-to-end
* Invent models for joint budget allocation, incrementality, and long-term value
* Take innovations from prototype to production serving live advertiser campaigns
* Raise the technical bar across scientists and engineers

  
Key job responsibilities  

* Define the long-term scientific vision for our RL Gym based training process focusing on campaign optimization and other advertising workflows

It is backed by a strong team of AI researchers from Stanford, MIT, Berkeley, Princeton, and CMU, who have conducted over five years of cutting-edge research on training embedding models. We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Palo Alto for our hybrid working model.

We are seeking a Staff Research Scientist to join our team and contribute to the development of next-generation AI models. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on challenging problems at the intersection of machine learning research and practical deployment of large neural networks.

This role can be based out of our Palo Alto office, or remotely in the United States.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Research Engineer, RL Environments
jobs.description:
**About Us**
============

Preference Model is a superintelligence data research company. We build RL environments for training capable, better-aligned superintelligences.

Almost every aspect of how a model behaves is shaped by the reward signals it's trained on. The biggest problem with AIs today is that they don't always do what we intend. Sometimes that's because they aren't capable enough, and sometimes it's because they aren't aligned. Both problems come down to the training objectives.

We're trying to address both of these issues in the most direct, highest leverage way available to us, which today means researching how to build RL environments better, not just for the AIs of today but for the AIs as they will be when they outsmart us.

Over the past year, we've built RL environments for several frontier labs, and we're backed by $16M in seed funding led by a16z. Our founding team has previous experience on Anthropic’s data team building data infrastructure, and datasets behind Claude.

**About the Role**
==================

We’re hiring experienced **Machine Learning Engineers** to design and build **reinforcement learning environments** to safely advance model capabilities in machine learning research and engineering. Specifically, you'll be teaching frontier models to do the work of an ML engineer or researcher at a frontier lab.

This role blends **research and engineering**. It will require you to stay up to date with the latest research, develop novel approaches, and realize them in code. You will have full ownership and autonomy of the environments you build. Your work will include designing and implementing RL environments, conducting experiments and evaluations, delivering your work into production training runs, and collaborating with other researchers and engineers.

You will join our Capabilities org, a small, high-ownership team and contribute directly to the data layer that powers frontier LLM capability.

**Note:** This role is only for **experienced ML Engineers**. We have a separate opening for New Grads.

**What You Will Do:**
=====================

* Design and build RL environments and reward functions that produce clean, learnable signals for frontier models on ML research and engineering tasks
* Build deep expertise across the frontier of ML research, training, and inference infrastructure
* Collaborate with others to brainstorm and create new ideas and tools to improve the environment building process

**What We are Looking For (Qualifications):**
=============================================

* 5+ years of experience working in machine learning or research, primarily on LLMs and transformer models
* You have strong ML fundamentals and broad research interests. You read many papers or tutorials, understand topics deeply and have the creativity to translate them into RLVR problems
* Proficiency in Python and systems programming and at least one of PyTorch or JAX
* Problem solvers who take ownership and drives solutions end-to-end
* Passion for staying current with the rapidly evolving ML infrastructure landscape
* Ability to meet throughput expectations and respond quickly to feedback

**You may be a good fit if you also:**
--------------------------------------

* Have expert knowledge in an active DL/ML research area, with publications or public code to show for it. Research experience (PhD, MS) is a big plus
* Have deep understanding of transformer internals, training/inference of modern LLMs, experience with inference libraries (vLLM, SGLang, etc)
* Have strong expertise in kernel development (CUDA, Triton, Pallas)
* Have built complex interactive RL environments

**What We Offer:**
==================

* Competitive cash and equity compensation (>90th percentile)
* Ownership and autonomy in a fast moving startup environment
* Opportunity to work with top machine learning engineers
* Health, vision, dental, benefits
* 401K match
* Lunch provided everyday onsite
* Weekly snack orders
* Visa sponsorship & relocation support available

**We value diverse perspectives and experiences. If you're excited about this role but don't check every box, we still encourage you to apply.**

Compensation Range: $200K - $350K
